subproblems.title: Local Lipschitz bounds along a segment give the global bound (parent step 6a)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (Euclid P), x, y ∈ ℝ^P and K ≥ 0. Suppose that for every t ∈ [0, 1], with w_t := x + t(y − x), there is a neighbourhood U of w_t such that |f(w) − f(w_t)| ≤ K|w − w_t| for all w ∈ U. Then |f(y) − f(x)| ≤ K|y − x|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P) (x y : Euclid P) (K : ℝ), 0 ≤ K → (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝 (x + t • (y - x)), dist (f w) (f (x + t • (y - x))) ≤ K * dist w (x + t • (y - x))) → dist (f y) (f x) ≤ K * dist y x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (6a) of the supplied proof of the selected parent dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_retraction [its parent's Lemma D = Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4, with the documented 3/4 → 1/4 erratum]: f(t) := ψ(x + t(y − x)), t* := sup{t ∈ [0, 1] : |f(s) − f(0)| ≤ ((2c₁/r)|y − x| + ε)s for all s ≤ t}, the bound holds at t* by continuity and extends past t*. In the parent the local bound of step 5 holds as an inequality on a neighbourhood of each point of the segment, which is the hypothesis here; so the parent's ε is not needed.
1. Put D := |y − x| and g(t) := x + t(y − x) (t ∈ ℝ). Then g(0) = x, g(1) = y, g is continuous and |g(s) − g(t)| = |s − t|·D.
2. Continuity of f ∘ g on [0, 1]. Fix t ∈ [0, 1] and let U be the neighbourhood of g(t) given by the hypothesis. Since g is continuous, g(s) ∈ U for all s close to t, and then |f(g(s)) − f(g(t))| ≤ K|g(s) − g(t)| = K·D·|s − t| → 0 as s → t. Hence f ∘ g is continuous at every t ∈ [0, 1] (squeeze), and h(t) := |f(g(t)) − f(x)| − K·t·D is continuous on [0, 1].
3. Let S := {t ∈ ℝ : |f(g(t)) − f(x)| ≤ K·t·D}. Then S ∩ [0, 1] = [0, 1] ∩ h⁻¹((−∞, 0]) is closed, because h is continuous on the closed set [0, 1] (ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed).
4. 0 ∈ S, because g(0) = x and |f(x) − f(x)| = 0 = K·0·D.
5. Right extension. Let t ∈ S ∩ [0, 1). With U as in 2, choose δ > 0 such that g(s) ∈ U whenever |s − t| < δ. For s ∈ (t, t + δ): |f(g(s)) − f(x)| ≤ |f(g(s)) − f(g(t))| + |f(g(t)) − f(x)| ≤ K(s − t)D + K·t·D = K·s·D, so s ∈ S. Thus (t, t + δ) ⊆ S, i.e. S ∈ 𝓝[>] t.
6. By the continuous induction principle on [0, 1] (Mathlib IsClosed.Icc_subset_of_forall_mem_nhdsWithin, applied with 3, 4 and 5), [0, 1] ⊆ S. This is the parent's argument: t* := sup{t ∈ [0, 1] : [0, t] ⊆ S} lies in S by 3, and t* < 1 would contradict 5.
7. In particular 1 ∈ S: |f(y) − f(x)| = |f(g(1)) − f(x)| ≤ K·1·D = K|y − x|. (The degenerate cases x = y and K = 0 are covered by the same argument.) ∎

subproblems.title: The closed unit cubes containing a point cover a neighbourhood of it (parent steps 5 and 6)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P). There is a finite set Z ⊆ ℤ^P such that x ∈ z + [0,1]^P (i.e. z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for all i) for every z ∈ Z, and every y in some neighbourhood of x lies in z + [0,1]^P for some z ∈ Z.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (x : Euclid P), ∃ Z : Finset (Fin P → ℤ), (∀ z ∈ Z, ∀ i, (z i : ℝ) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ z i + 1) ∧ ∀ᶠ y : Euclid P in 𝓝 x, ∃ z ∈ Z, ∀ i, (z i : ℝ) ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ z i + 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_retraction [its parent's Lemma D = Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4, with the documented 3/4 → 1/4 erratum]: 'The closed unit cubes not containing x form a closed set missing x, so points y near x lie in the finitely many closed cubes containing x' (used for D̄ψ(x) ≤ max over those cubes, and again through step 5 in step 6). This child proves that local finiteness fact by an explicit coordinatewise construction.
1. One-dimensional claim. For t ∈ ℝ let A(t) := {k ∈ {⌊t⌋ − 1, ⌊t⌋} : k ≤ t ≤ k + 1} and V(t) := ⋃_{k ∈ A(t)} [k, k + 1]. Then V(t) is a neighbourhood of t. If t ∉ ℤ, then ⌊t⌋ < t < ⌊t⌋ + 1, so ⌊t⌋ ∈ A(t) and V(t) ⊇ (⌊t⌋, ⌊t⌋ + 1) ∋ t. If t ∈ ℤ, then ⌊t⌋ = t, both t − 1 and t lie in A(t), and V(t) ⊇ [t − 1, t + 1] ⊇ (t − 1, t + 1) ∋ t. (Int.floor_le, Int.lt_floor_add_one.)
2. Let Z be the set of z ∈ ℤ^P with z_i ∈ {⌊x_i⌋ − 1, ⌊x_i⌋} and z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for all i. It is a subset of the finite product ∏_i {⌊x_i⌋ − 1, ⌊x_i⌋} (Fintype.piFinset, then Finset.filter), hence a Finset, and by construction x ∈ z + [0,1]^P for every z ∈ Z. This is the first conclusion. (For P = 0, Z is the singleton of the unique element of ℤ^0 and every condition below is vacuous.)
3. For each coordinate i the map y ↦ y_i is continuous, so by 1 the set W_i := {y : y_i ∈ V(x_i)} is a neighbourhood of x. Since there are finitely many coordinates, eventually in 𝓝 x the point y lies in W_i for all i simultaneously (Filter.eventually_all).
4. Let y ∈ W_i for all i. For each i choose k_i ∈ A(x_i) with k_i ≤ y_i ≤ k_i + 1 (possible because y_i ∈ V(x_i)) and put z := (k_i)_i. Then z_i ∈ {⌊x_i⌋ − 1, ⌊x_i⌋} and z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for every i, so z ∈ Z, and z_i ≤ y_i ≤ z_i + 1 for every i. This is the second conclusion. ∎

Let L*(a) := {w ∈ ℝ^P : there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with |s| ≥ m + 2 and w_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s} and d := infDist(x, L*(a)) (Metric.infDist, which is 0 for the empty set). subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_retraction [its parent's Lemma D = Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4, with the documented 3/4 → 1/4 erratum]: the centre a + b of the cube G = b + C and the cone K_G of its closing Remark (the planes {u : u_i = b_i + a_i (i ∈ J')}, J' ⊆ {1, …, P}, |J'| = n + 1 = m + 2, through that centre; in step (5b) the corresponding cone is K₀) lie in L*(a), so d(x) ≤ dist(x, K_G). This child is the coordinate form of that comparison; in the parent assembly it starts the sibling face_induction on the cube b + C with ρ := d(x)/√(m + 2). No hypothesis on a is needed.
1. Put d := infDist(x, L*(a)) ≥ 0 and S := {i : |x_i − b_i − a_i| < d/√(m + 2)}. Suppose, for a contradiction, that |S| ≥ m + 2, and choose s ⊆ S with |s| = m + 2 (Finset.exists_subset_card_eq).
2. Define w ∈ ℝ^P by w_i := b_i + a_i for i ∈ s and w_i := x_i for i ∉ s (WithLp.toLp). For i ∈ s, w_i − a_i = b_i ∈ ℤ, and |s| = m + 2, so w ∈ L*(a) (w lies on the plane of K_G with J' = s). Hence d ≤ |x − w| (Metric.infDist_le_dist_of_mem).
3. By EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, |x − w|² = Σ_i (x_i − w_i)² = Σ_{i ∈ s} (x_i − b_i − a_i)². For i ∈ s we have 0 ≤ |x_i − b_i − a_i| < d/√(m + 2), so (x_i − b_i − a_i)² < d²/(m + 2). Since s has m + 2 ≥ 1 elements, summing gives |x − w|² < (m + 2)·d²/(m + 2) = d², hence |x − w| < d (both sides are nonnegative).
4. Steps 2 and 3 give d ≤ |x − w| < d, a contradiction. Hence |S| ≤ m + 1. (If d = 0, S is empty, and the conclusion is immediate; the argument above covers this case too.) ∎

subproblems.title: Radial retraction of a face from its centre: gauge bounds, boundary values, radial estimate (parent steps 1 and 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and a ∈ ℝ^P with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i. Let b ∈ ℤ^P and J a nonempty set of coordinate indices, F := F(b, J) = {y : b_k ≤ y_k ≤ b_k + 1 (k ∈ J), y_k = b_k (k ∉ J)}. For y ∈ ℝ^P let N(y) := max_{k ∈ J} max((y_k − b_k − a_k)/(1 − a_k), (b_k + a_k − y_k)/a_k). This is the gauge of F − a_F at y − a_F, where a_F has coordinates b_k + a_k on J and b_k off J. Let ψ_F : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be any map with ψ_F(y)_i = b_i + a_i + (y_i − b_i − a_i)/N(y) for i ∈ J and ψ_F(y)_i = y_i for i ∉ J. Let x ∈ F with x_i ≠ b_i + a_i for some i ∈ J. 1. For every y and every k ∈ J, |t_k(y)| ≤ g_y(k) ≤ N(y). If t := t_k(y) ≥ 0, then t/(1 − a_k) ≥ t = |t| because 0 < 1 − a_k ≤ 1. If t < 0, then −t/a_k ≥ −t = |t| because 0 < a_k ≤ 1. Finally g_y(k) ≤ N(y) since k ∈ J (Finset.le_sup'). With y = x this is (1).

Notation. For b ∈ ℤ^P and a finite index set J, F(b, J) := {u : b_i ≤ u_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ J), u_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}. For J ≠ ∅ let R_{b,J} : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the map (built with WithLp.toLp) with R_{b,J}(u)_i = b_i + a_i + (u_i − b_i − a_i)/N_{b,J}(u) for i ∈ J and R_{b,J}(u)_i = u_i for i ∉ J, where N_{b,J}(u) = max_{k ∈ J} max((u_k − b_k − a_k)/(1 − a_k), (b_k + a_k − u_k)/a_k) (Finset.sup'; its value does not depend on the nonemptiness proof). For J = ∅ let R_{b,J} := id. For J ≠ ∅, R_{b,J} satisfies the coordinate hypothesis on ψF in the sibling face_radial; R_{b,J} is the parent's ψ_F for F = F(b, J).
1. Boundary lemma. Let |J| = |J'|, u ∈ F(b, J) ∩ F(b', J') and (b, J) ≠ (b', J'). Then u_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} for some i ∈ J.
 Proof. If J ≠ J', then J ⊄ J' (a subset of the same finite cardinality would be equal), so pick i ∈ J ∖ J'. Then u_i = b'_i ∈ ℤ and b_i ≤ u_i ≤ b_i + 1, and the only integers in [b_i, b_i + 1] are b_i and b_i + 1.
 If J = J', then b_i ≠ b'_i for some i. The case i ∉ J is impossible, since then b_i = u_i = b'_i. So i ∈ J and u_i ∈ [b_i, b_i + 1] ∩ [b'_i, b'_i + 1]. If b'_i ≥ b_i + 1 then b_i + 1 ≤ b'_i ≤ u_i ≤ b_i + 1, so u_i = b_i + 1; if b'_i ≤ b_i − 1 then b_i ≤ u_i ≤ b'_i + 1 ≤ b_i, so u_i = b_i. Either way u_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1}.
 By symmetry, u_{i'} ∈ {b'_{i'}, b'_{i'} + 1} for some i' ∈ J'.
2. Consistency. If |J| = |J'| ≥ 1 and u ∈ F(b, J) ∩ F(b', J'), then R_{b,J}(u) = R_{b',J'}(u). If (b, J) = (b', J') this is trivial. Otherwise, by 1, u has a coordinate i ∈ J with u_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1}. From |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 we get 1/4 < a_i < 3/4, so u_i ≠ b_i + a_i; hence face_radial applies to the face (b, J), the map R_{b,J} and the point u, and its conclusion (5) (ψF x = x at boundary points) gives R_{b,J}(u) = u. In the same way R_{b',J'}(u) = u.
3. Step maps (the parent's ψ^{(j)}). For j ∈ ℕ and u ∈ ℝ^P: if some pair (b', J') with |J'| = j satisfies u ∈ F(b', J'), choose such a pair p_j(u) (classical choice) and put φ_j(u) := R_{p_j(u)}(u). Otherwise put φ_j(u) := u.
4. The composite (the parent's ψ = ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)}, n = m + 1). Define Ψ by recursion on k: Ψ_k := id for k ≤ m + 1, and Ψ_k := Ψ_{k−1} ∘ φ_k for k ≥ m + 2. Then Ψ_{m+1} = id, and Ψ_j(u) = Ψ_{j−1}(φ_j(u)) for every j ≥ m + 2 and every u.

All coordinates of y and R_{b,J}(x) agree (the nonemptiness proof inside Finset.sup' is irrelevant), so y = R_{b,J}(x) (PiLp.ext); this includes the centre x = a_F, where N_{b,J}(x) = 0, division by 0 gives 0 and y = x = R_{b,J}(x). The pair (b, J) shows that the choice in 3 is made, so φ_j(x) = R_p(x) for some p = (b', J') with |J'| = j ≥ 1 and x ∈ F(b', J'). By 2, R_p(x) = R_{b,J}(x) = y. Hence Ψ_j(x) = Ψ_{j−1}(φ_j(x)) = Ψ_{j−1}(y). ∎

- F(b, J) := {u : b_i ≤ u_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ J), u_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}, with centre a_F (coordinates b_i + a_i on J, b_i off J);
- for J ≠ ∅, N_{b,J}(u) := max_{k ∈ J} max((u_k − b_k − a_k)/(1 − a_k), (b_k + a_k − u_k)/a_k) (Finset.sup'; independent of the nonemptiness proof);
- ψ_{b,J} : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is the map (built with WithLp.toLp) with ψ_{b,J}(u)_i = b_i + a_i + (u_i − b_i − a_i)/N_{b,J}(u) for i ∈ J and ψ_{b,J}(u)_i = u_i for i ∉ J; it satisfies the coordinate hypothesis on ψF in face_radial;
- for u ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0, C(b, J, u, ρ) means #{i ∈ J : |u_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ} ≤ m + 1.
REC denotes the recursion hypothesis on Ψ. Applied with y := ψ_{b,J}(u), whose coordinates are exactly the required ones, it gives Ψ_j(u) = Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_{b,J}(u)) whenever m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, |J| = j and u ∈ F(b, J).
Put K := 1 + 4√P ≥ 1 and c := K^P > 0; c depends only on P (in particular only on P and m).
Claim(j), for m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P: for all b, all J with |J| = j, all x ∈ F(b, J) and all ρ > 0 with C(b, J, x, ρ):
 (A) Ψ_j(x) ∈ F(b, J);
 (B) there is a set s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and Ψ_j(x)_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s;

0. Claim(j) for all j ∈ [m + 2, P] gives the theorem with this c. (A) and (B) are its first two conclusions. Because K ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ j − m − 1 ≤ P, K^{j−m−1} ≤ K^P = c, so (C) gives dist(Ψ_j y, Ψ_j x) ≤ (c/ρ)·dist(y, x) for all y ∈ F(b, J) with dist(y, x) < δ, i.e. eventually in 𝓝[F(b, J)] x (Metric.mem_nhdsWithin_iff). If m + 2 > P there is nothing to prove. Claim(j) is proved by induction on j starting at m + 2 (Nat.le_induction), carrying the hypothesis j ≤ P (if j + 1 ≤ P then j ≤ P).
1. Preliminaries. Fix j with m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, b, J with |J| = j (so J ≠ ∅), F := F(b, J), x ∈ F and ρ > 0 with C(b, J, x, ρ). Write N := N_{b,J} and ψ_F := ψ_{b,J}.
 (a) Since |J| = j ≥ m + 2 > m + 1, some i ∈ J has |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≥ ρ > 0 (otherwise all j indices of J would be counted). In particular x_i ≠ b_i + a_i, so face_radial applies to x, and by its conclusion (1), N(x) ≥ |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≥ ρ.
 (b) If y ∈ F and |y − x| < ρ/2, then C(b, J, y, ρ/2) holds. Indeed, if |y_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ/2, then |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≤ |x_i − y_i| + |y_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ/2 + ρ/2 = ρ, since |x_i − y_i| ≤ |x − y| (PiLp.dist_apply_le). So the set counted for (y, ρ/2) is contained in the set counted for (x, ρ). Applying (a) to y and ρ/2: y_i ≠ b_i + a_i for some i ∈ J.
 (c) By REC, Ψ_j(u) = Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_F(u)) for every u ∈ F.
 (d) By face_radial at x: 0 < N(x) ≤ 1; ψ_F(x) ∈ F; ψ_F(x)_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} for some i ∈ J; and |ψ_F(y) − ψ_F(x)| ≤ (1 + 4√j)/N(x)·|y − x| for every y ∈ F with y_i ≠ b_i + a_i for some i ∈ J, in particular, by (b), for every y ∈ F with |y − x| < ρ/2. For every such y, face_radial at y gives ψ_F(y) ∈ F and ψ_F(y)_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} for some i ∈ J.
2. Base case j = m + 2 (the Remark's case j = n + 1, where L*(a) ∩ G = {a_G}). By (c) and Ψ_{m+1} = id, Ψ_j(u) = ψ_F(u) for every u ∈ F.
 (A) Ψ_j(x) = ψ_F(x) ∈ F by 1(d).
 (B) Take i₀ ∈ J with ψ_F(x)_{i₀} ∈ {b_{i₀}, b_{i₀} + 1} (1(d)) and let s := (all indices ∖ J) ∪ {i₀}. For i ∉ J, ψ_F(x)_i = x_i = b_i ∈ ℤ, and ψ_F(x)_{i₀} ∈ ℤ. Since i₀ ∈ J, |s| = (P − (m + 2)) + 1, so P = m + 1 + |s|.
 (C) Take δ := ρ/2. For y ∈ F with |y − x| < δ, 1(d), N(x) ≥ ρ from 1(a), and m + 2 ≤ P give |Ψ_j(y) − Ψ_j(x)| = |ψ_F(y) − ψ_F(x)| ≤ (1 + 4√(m + 2))/N(x)·|y − x| ≤ (K/ρ)|y − x|, and K = K^{j−m−1}.
3. Inductive step: m + 3 ≤ j ≤ P, and Claim(j − 1) holds. Put y₀ := ψ_F(x) and λ := 1/N(x) > 0. By the formula for ψ_F, y₀_k − b_k − a_k = λ(x_k − b_k − a_k) for k ∈ J (the Remark's y₀ = a_G + λ(y − a_G)) and y₀_k = x_k = b_k for k ∉ J. By (c), Ψ_j(x) = Ψ_{j−1}(y₀).
 (i) Faces through y₀. For i ∈ J and an integer β ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} put b^{i,β} := b with the i-th entry replaced by β (Function.update), J^i := J ∖ {i} (so |J^i| = j − 1 ≥ m + 2), and G_{i,β} := F(b^{i,β}, J^i). Then G_{i,β} ⊆ F: for u ∈ G_{i,β}, b_k ≤ u_k ≤ b_k + 1 for k ∈ J^i, u_i = β ∈ [b_i, b_i + 1], and u_k = b_k for k ∉ J. If y₀_i = β, then y₀ ∈ G_{i,β}: b_k ≤ y₀_k ≤ b_k + 1 for k ∈ J^i since y₀ ∈ F, y₀_i = β, and y₀_k = b_k for k ∉ J. By 1(d) at least one pair (i, β) with y₀_i = β exists, and there are at most 2j pairs in all.
 (ii) Scaling (the Remark's dist(y₀, K_G) = λ·dist(y, K_G)). If y₀_i = β, then C(b^{i,β}, J^i, y₀, λρ) holds. For k ∈ J^i, b^{i,β}_k = b_k and |y₀_k − b_k − a_k| = λ|x_k − b_k − a_k|, which is < λρ iff |x_k − b_k − a_k| < ρ, since λ > 0. So the counted set is a subset of the one for (b, J, x, ρ), which has at most m + 1 elements.
 (iii) For every pair with y₀_i = β apply Claim(j − 1) to (b^{i,β}, J^i, y₀, λρ). Its (A) gives Ψ_{j−1}(y₀) ∈ G_{i,β} ⊆ F; this is (A) for Ψ_j(x) = Ψ_{j−1}(y₀). Its (B) is (B) for Ψ_j(x). Its (C) gives δ_{i,β} > 0 such that |Ψ_{j−1}(y') − Ψ_{j−1}(y₀)| ≤ (K^{j−m−2}/(λρ))|y' − y₀| = (K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ)|y' − y₀| for all y' ∈ G_{i,β} with |y' − y₀| < δ_{i,β}.
 (iv) Nearby boundary points lie on faces through y₀ (parent: every face meeting B_δ(y₀) contains y₀). Choose η > 0 with η ≤ δ_{i,β} for every pair with y₀_i = β and η ≤ |y₀_i − β| for every pair (i ∈ J, β ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1}) with y₀_i ≠ β; for instance the minimum of these finitely many positive numbers and 1.
 (v) Put δ := min(ρ/2, η·N(x)/(1 + 4√j)) > 0. For y ∈ F with |y − x| < δ, 1(d) gives |ψ_F(y) − y₀| ≤ (1 + 4√j)/N(x)·|y − x| < η.
 (vi) Let y ∈ F with |y − x| < δ. By (c), Ψ_j(y) = Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_F(y)). By 1(d) (note |y − x| < ρ/2), ψ_F(y) ∈ F and ψ_F(y)_i = β for some i ∈ J and some β ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1}. If y₀_i ≠ β, then |y₀_i − β| = |y₀_i − ψ_F(y)_i| ≤ |y₀ − ψ_F(y)| < η ≤ |y₀_i − β|, which is impossible; so y₀_i = β and (i, β) is one of the pairs in (iii). Then ψ_F(y) ∈ G_{i,β}: its coordinates k ∈ J^i lie in [b_k, b_k + 1] because ψ_F(y) ∈ F, its i-th coordinate is β, and ψ_F(y)_k = y_k = b_k for k ∉ J. Since |ψ_F(y) − y₀| < η ≤ δ_{i,β}, (iii) and (v) give (the Remark's chain rule)
 |Ψ_j(y) − Ψ_j(x)| = |Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_F(y)) − Ψ_{j−1}(y₀)| ≤ (K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ)·|ψ_F(y) − y₀| ≤ (K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ)·((1 + 4√j)/N(x))·|y − x| ≤ (K^{j−m−1}/ρ)|y − x|,
 because 1 + 4√j ≤ 1 + 4√P = K. This is (C) of Claim(j) with this δ.
4. By induction Claim(j) holds for all m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, and step 0 gives the theorem. ∎
